<u>NBC 6 SOUTH FLORIDA</u>: 10 Sentenced in South Florida Cocaine Conspiracy Linked to Mexican Cartel
August 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Ten people who moved cocaine through Florida get up to 15 years. The ring ran inside the US, 2024–2025 — but the byline hook is "Mexican cartel," the same reflex that made a Cambodia bust a Sinaloa story this same week.

🇲🇽 The man "sent to oversee" the network drew a 5-year sentence; the domestic supply chain rarely gets the billing its foreign label does.

• Sentences "up to 15 years and eight months"
• Cocaine "supplied by a Mexican cartel"

<u>AP</u>: Cambodia-US Operation Uncovers Money Laundering Link to Sinaloa Cartel
August 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A crypto-laundering network dismantled in Cambodia — $7M in seized crypto, 200kg of drugs, a metric ton of precursor chemicals. The proper noun in the headline, 8,000 miles from Mexico? 🔍 "Sinaloa Cartel."

🇲🇽 Cambodian police and the DEA made the arrests in Cambodia; the "Mexican cartel" tag is the device that turns a Southeast Asian bust into a Mexico story.

• "$7 million in cryptocurrency linked to the Sinaloa Cartel"
• Over one metric ton of precursor chemicals seized — in Cambodia

<u>REUTERS</u>: Governor Indicted by US on Cartel Charges Requests Leave Again
August 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Sinaloa's Rubén Rocha Moya reclaimed his post Friday — 34 hours later he was gone again. What forced him out wasn't Washington. It was his own side: Morena and Sheinbaum told him to step aside, and he did.

🇲🇽 The US indictment naming him has never been tested in court, and Mexico says Washington never handed over evidence to justify an arrest or extradition.

• Sheinbaum: "power without principles becomes arrogance"
• Morena accused him of putting "personal interests above those of the people"

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's heavy-vehicle exports jumped 66.7% in July</u>

Mexico shipped 13,117 trucks and buses abroad in July, up 66.7% from a year earlier, while production climbed 51.8% to 14,675 units, per ANPACT data reported by El Economista. The US absorbed 92.4% of those exports — Washington's "tariff war" hasn't loosened American industry's dependence on Mexican-built heavy vehicles.

🇲🇽📚 <u>Sheinbaum defends handing school budgets straight to parents, not contractors</u>

Sheinbaum rejected a PAN proposal to route La Escuela es Nuestra funds through municipal governments, defending the model that gives parent committees the money directly for school upkeep. "100,000 pesos delivered to parents yields more results than private contractors," she said, noting that fewer than 1% of cases have shown any administrative problem. The opposition wants the money back in the middlemen's hands.
banner: SCHOOL CASH GOES STRAIGHT TO PARENTS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Declassified files describe the PRI's "technocratic" era as a narco-state run from the top</u>

A Contralínea investigation, citing Sedena military reports and a February 2000 CIA assessment, lays out how the "modernizing" governments of Salinas and Zedillo fused presidential power with the cartels. A 1995 V Región Militar document logs Amado Carrillo's "Christmas gifts" to a Zedillo campaign aide; Raúl Salinas was jailed over $100M in Swiss accounts; García Ábrego was expelled under Article 33 as "the capo without a nation." The CIA itself called Mexico a "narco-state" with "untouchable" figures — the same technocrats the opposition now sells as democratic elders.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's self-appointed "electoral watchdogs" are 30+ opposition NGOs, some funded by the US Embassy</u>

A Contralínea investigation maps ANIE, the "electoral integrity" bloc formed in 2023 under the previous Electoral Tribunal: 30+ organizations including Coparmex, Causa en Común and groups tied to Claudio X. González's network. Causa en Común is funded by the US Embassy's narcotics bureau and the National Endowment for Democracy. The bloc filed 300+ "complaints" against López Obrador and issued four reports pressuring the INE over the 2024 election Morena won by a landslide.
banner: US-FUNDED NGOs POSE AS VOTE WATCHDOGS

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Milei's digital operative planned to "wreck" Mexico's 2027 elections, ex-partner says</u>

Fernando Cerimedo — co-founder of La Derecha Diario, brought to Mexico by Ricardo Salinas Pliego last December — told his ex-partner "I'm going to wreck it in the elections, because he hates the President," she told the press from a Bolivian hospital where she's recovering from an attack he allegedly ordered. Bolivian prosecutors raiding his La Paz properties found a bot farm, dozens of phones and more than half a million bolivianos in cash.
banner: MILEI OPERATIVE PLOTTED TO WRECK 2027 VOTE

text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sinaloa's governor lasted 34 hours back in office before quitting again</u>

Rubén Rocha Moya returned to the Sinaloa governorship after 112 days of leave — then requested indefinite leave again just 34 hours later, once Sheinbaum and Morena publicly distanced themselves. His original May 1 exit followed a US accusation naming him and 9 other officials over alleged ties to a Sinaloa cartel faction — an accusation Washington has never backed with a single charge in a Mexican court.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexican formal wages hit their highest level on record</u>

The average wage registered with the IMSS reached 673.9 pesos a day in July — the highest on record, up 42.4 pesos over the year, per El Economista — with 22.76 million formal jobs on the books, the most ever for a July. A seasonal dip in headcount, driven by the end of the school year and the harvest cycle, didn't touch the wage floor that keeps climbing under the 4T.
